root_cause: CORRECTED 2026-10-08 (retraction recorded below): a RANKING failure, not absence. All 11 .proto files ARE in the index — 79 records in the opentelemetry-proto-docs dataset (metrics.proto 22, profiles.proto 21, trace.proto 11, logs.proto 7, common.proto 5, six service/context/resource files 2-3 each), assigned via the txt-lines family per the dry-run plan (family txt-lines, assignment opentelemetry-proto-docs). The needle text is retrievable: match_phrase on text for 'An ID with all zeroes OR' returns trace.proto and logs.proto at score 9.1. But txt-lines chunks a 368-line definition file into 11 records of ~2KB, so the BM25 mass of the query terms the file matches is split across fragments, while each semantic-conventions .md file competes as a whole document; a fragment carrying a subset of the terms cannot outscore long prose matching more of them. Measured on the re-run (unchanged suite, /tmp/xtarget-fam binary, :19295): query 1's needle chunk ranks 19th of 50 at 17.99 against a top-5 cutoff of 23.14. Every proto-needled query's top-5 is semconv .md prose (2,464 whole-document records vs 79 proto fragments). RETRACTED root cause (kept for the record): the first grading claimed the needle files were absent, on two probes — the terminal line's code_files=0 and a wildcard ax_file=*trace.proto returning zero. Both were misread: ax_file stores the content digest, not the filename (the trap documented in the #1183 era), so a filename wildcard answers zero by construction; the correct presence probe is ax_path, which returns 79 records. code_files=0 is a labeling gap (a definitions file is not a tree-sitter code file) and it fed the misdiagnosis.
next: engine issue #1254 retitled to the real defect: definition-format files fall to txt-lines line-chunking and cannot compete with whole-document prose, and the terminal line reports code_files=0 for them. Fix direction: a code-family route for .proto (tree-sitter-proto exists on crates.io) or a whole-document text route for structured non-log text; then rebuild the corpus and re-run this suite unchanged. otel-proto stays candidate — flipping it live on markdown-only retrieval would misrepresent the corpus, whose point is the protocol definitions.
